newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell commercial aircraft profit up.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell commercial aircraft profit up.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp said Thursday that operating earnings for its commercial aircraft segment were $101 million in 1996, including $41 million in the fourth quarter.
Excluding a charge related to the MD-11 trijet, commercial aircraft operating earnings for 1995 were $39.0 million, including $13.0 million in the 1995 third quarter.
Earnings from the sale of spare parts and related services continued to make a significant contribution to earnings in 1996, McDonnell said.
Operating earnings on aircraft production programs, although improved in 1996 from 1995, were near break-even.

Commercial aircraft earnings in the fourth quarter of 1996 improved from the 1995 period, due largely to an increase in the number of MD-90 deliveries in 1996 and the inclusion of an MD-80 inventory write-off in 1995, it said.
Revenues for commercial aircraft were $3.3 billion for all of 1996, down from $3.9 billion in 1995. Fourth quarter revenues were $1.4 billion, up from $900,000 a year earlier.
McDonnell said it received orders for 10 MD-80 twin jets and three MD-11 trijets in the 1996 fourth quarter.
On December 31 it had firm orders for 29 MD-80 twin jets, 105 MD-90 twin jets, 50 MD-95 twin jets, and 15 MD-11 trijets.
Financial Services and other operating earnings were $74 million for 1996, up from $61 million in 1995, and for the fourth quarter they rose to $20 million from $19 million a year ago.

Operating earnings for missiles, space and electronics systems were $194 million for 1996, down from $198 million for 1995, but for the fourth quarter they rose to $40 million from $30 million a year ago.
Revenues for missiles, space and electronics rose to $2.2 billion for 1996 from $1.9 billion in 1995, but in the fourth quarter they fell to $508.0 million from $551 million a year earlier.
